newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy says Albania elections must be legitimate.
newsitem.headline: Italy says Albania elections must be legitimate.

text.p: Italy's defence minister Beniamino Andreatta said on Thursday that the process leading up to the Albanian elections in June must be legitimate otherwise the international community might rethink its readiness to help the country out of crisis.
European envoy Franz Vranitzky announced on Thursday that Albania's political parties had agreed to go ahead with a general election on June 29.
"If Vranitzky can guarantee the international community that the electoral process remains correct the interest of the (international) community in Albania stands," he told reporters.

"If the electoral process is delegitimised because half of the Albanian political forces...cast doubt on the correctness of this process, it will be difficult for the international community to continue to carry out its functions, including the military one...," he said.
Italy is leading a multinational force in Albania with about 6,000 troops.

"It is up to Albanians to decide if they want to save Albania," Andreatta said. "There is a danger that the situation that will be created in Albania is a delegitimisation of the government born from these elections," he said.

Vranitzky, mediating in Albania for the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) since widespread violence erupted in March, said the parties had agreed to elect 115 seats by majority voting and 40 seats through a proportional system.
The 54-nation OSCE would give its total support to help in preparing the election and would send as many observers as was deemed necessary, together with the Council of Europe, Vranitzky said.
"We will help Albania. The whole international community is speaking with unanimity. There are no dissenting voices," Vranitzky added.
